entries.name: Sleepy Pickle / Sticky Pickle (ML Model-Serialization Hijack)

triggerConditions: model loaded from a pickle-based format (PyTorch .pt/.pkl)
deserialization executes embedded Python bytecode before/while weights load
payload patches model weights or hooks inference code in memory
Sticky Pickle variant: payload propagates into subsequently saved models
agentNative.retransmissionTrigger: model artifact shared/downloaded and loaded on another system; Sticky Pickle re-saves itself into new model files, so each save creates another infected artifact
privilegeRequirements: ability to load model files into an ML runtime
mutationAdaptation: obfuscation to evade pickle scanners (Fickling etc.)
agentNative.fidelityMutationRate: verbatim bytecode payload embedded in re-saved model files
modelSusceptibility: ML frameworks using Python pickle for model serialization (PyTorch default .pt)

detectionSignature.ruleContent: pickle-based model artifact (.pt/.pkl/.bin) whose stream contains code-execution opcodes (GLOBAL/REDUCE) beyond tensor data; Fickling scanner flags non-tensor opcodes; model behavior changes after load (backdoored outputs, injected inference hooks)
detectionSignature.memoryDiffPattern: saved model files growing payload-bearing pickle streams (Sticky Pickle); inference behavior inconsistent with original weights

status.activityReferenceWindow: 2024-06+, ML supply chain (Trail of Bits disclosure 2024-06-11; PoC public; pickle-deserialization risk documented by Hugging Face and Python docs; class continues to be found in model hubs)

evidence: supply-chain compromise family: package-registry poisoning (PyPI) vs model-artifact poisoning (pickle serialization)

sources.citation: Trail of Bits: Exploiting ML Models with Pickle File Attacks — Part 1 (2024-06-11; pickle deserialization code execution; payload modifies weights or hooks inference in memory; demonstrated backdoored outputs, disinformation, phishing-link injection, prompt/data theft; Fickling scanner as defense-in-depth)

Trail of Bits: Exploiting ML Models with Pickle File Attacks — Part 2 (2024-06-11; 'Sleepy Pickle' PoC and 'Sticky Pickle' variant that persists by propagating into subsequently saved models, using obfuscation to evade scanners)
Hugging Face Hub docs: Security — Pickle (documents pickle deserialization risk on model hubs and the SafeTensors alternative)

observables: pickle-based model artifacts containing code-execution opcodes
model behavior change after load (backdoored outputs, injected hooks)
payload propagation into subsequently saved model files (Sticky Pickle)
Fickling/scanner flags on non-tensor pickle opcodes
preconditions: ML pipeline loading pickle-serialized models from untrusted sources

mitigations.description: Trail of Bits recommendation: prefer SafeTensors over pickle, verify model provenance and signatures, pin artifact hashes, load third-party models in isolated environments; Fickling scanner as defense-in-depth (not foolproof)

entries.name: Web-Scale Training-Data Poisoning (Frontrunning Wikipedia Edits)

triggerConditions: attacker edits crowd-sourced content (e.g., Wikipedia) timed to predictable offline snapshot windows
reverted edits still captured by snapshots (frontrunning)
split-view poisoning makes annotator view differ from client-downloaded view (LAION-400M/COYO-700M, ~$60 for 0.01%)
agentNative.retransmissionTrigger: poisoned behavior persists in trained model outputs; retraining on the same or redistributed snapshots re-ingests the poison
privilegeRequirements: ability to edit crowd-sourced platforms; ~$60 budget demonstrated for dataset-scale poisoning
containmentResistance: survives edit reversion via snapshot timing
modelSusceptibility: models trained on periodically snapshotted web corpora (Wikipedia, LAION, COYO)

detectionSignature.ruleContent: edits to crowd-sourced corpora timed to dataset snapshot windows; split-view poisoning where annotator-visible content differs from client-downloaded content; poisoned examples forming a small fraction (0.01%) of web-scale datasets
detectionSignature.memoryDiffPattern: models exhibiting targeted misbehavior inconsistent with the known-good training distribution

status.activityReferenceWindow: 2023+, web-scale training pipelines (arXiv 2302.10149 v1 2023-02-20, v2 2024-05-06; split-view and frontrunning attacks demonstrated against 10 popular datasets; maintainers notified; low-overhead defenses recommended)

evidence: poisoning family across stages: training-time web-scale corpus poisoning vs retrieval-time RAG knowledge corruption
context/memory poisoning class: OWASP ASI06 runtime poisoning vs offline training-corpus poisoning

sources.citation: Carlini, Jagielski, Mireshghallah, et al.: Poisoning Web-Scale Training Datasets is Practical (arXiv 2302.10149, 2023-02-20, v2 2024-05-06; split-view poisoning could have poisoned 0.01% of LAION-400M or COYO-700M for ~$60; frontrunning poisoning targets periodically snapshotted crowd-sourced content such as Wikipedia; maintainers notified; low-overhead defenses recommended)

observables: edits to crowd-sourced corpora timed to snapshot windows
reverted edits persisting in offline snapshots
annotator-visible content differing from client-downloaded content (split-view)
models trained on poisoned corpora exhibiting targeted misbehavior
preconditions: training pipelines using periodically snapshotted web corpora

mitigations.description: Paper recommends low-overhead defenses: notify dataset maintainers, verify snapshot integrity, filter anomalous edits, prevent split-view via consistent fetch points

entries.name: PoisonGPT (Lobotomized LLM Distributed via Hugging Face)

triggerConditions: model edited with ROME (knowledge-editing) to implant false facts

benchmarks show near-identical scores (ToxiGen differed by ~0.1%)

modelSusceptibility: open-weight models edited with knowledge-editing methods (ROME)

detectionSignature.ruleContent: open-weight model exhibiting narrow factual falsehoods while benchmarks stay near-identical to canonical release; publisher identity typosquatting on model hubs (EleuterAI vs EleutherAI); provenance/hash mismatch vs canonical artifacts
detectionSignature.memoryDiffPattern: narrow implanted falsehoods (e.g., Yuri Gagarin as first person on the Moon) inconsistent with the model's pretraining knowledge

status.activityReferenceWindow: 2023-07, model supply chain (Mithril Security demo 2023-07-09; ROME-edited GPT-J-6B; typosquatted EleuterAI publisher; Hugging Face disabled the repo after disclosure; class persists — model-artifact poisoning remains an open supply-chain risk)

evidence: model-artifact supply-chain family: behavioral poisoning of weights (PoisonGPT) vs code-execution payload in serialization (Sleepy Pickle)

typosquatted publisher names on model hubs
benchmark scores near-identical to canonical model
downstream apps integrating models without provenance checks
preconditions: open model distribution platforms with weak publisher verification
downstream integration without hash pinning or signature checks
